note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypertension and palpitations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old male with longstanding hypertension since youth presents for follow-up. Patient reports recent emergency room visit in March with elevated blood pressure and palpitations, which he attributes to consuming several cups of coffee without breakfast and possible panic attack. He denies recurrence of palpitations since that time. Patient notes family history of hypertension and reports that his previous primary care doctor started him on a new combination medication approximately one month ago. He checks blood pressure daily at home, with recent readings ranging from 146-155 mmHg. He is attempting to reduce salt intake and exercises on treadmill when able. Currently on three antihypertensive medications at maximum doses with inadequate blood pressure control.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current palpitations, chest pain, or other cardiac symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension (since young age)

MEDICATIONS
1. Benicar HCT (olmesartan/hydrochlorothiazide) 40-25 mg daily
2. Amlodipine 10 mg daily
3. Spironolactone (newly initiated)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant for hypertension in multiple family members.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient lives with girlfriend. Exercises on treadmill intermittently. Attempting dietary salt reduction.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing 49-year-old male
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, regular rate and rhythm
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender throughout
Extremities: No ankle or foot edema; pulses intact

RESULTS
Potassium level one week ago: 4.0 mEq/L (normal)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Resistant hypertension on three maximal-dose antihypertensive agents with inadequate control. Patient started on spironolactone for possible hyperaldosteronism. Counseled on medication side effects including possible dizziness, gynecomastia, and electrolyte abnormalities. Emphasized importance of dietary salt restriction (goal <2000 mg/day, ideally 1500 mg/day), increased exercise (30 minutes most days), and DASH diet adherence. Provided patient education materials and heart.org resources. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks for blood pressure check and metabolic panel to monitor potassium and sodium levels. If inadequate response to spironolactone, will refer to resistant hypertension clinic for evaluation of secondary causes and consideration of renal denervation procedure.
